source.result: Paulo Mimoso, 3rd place, Regional Nice (17 Oct 2026).
source.note: A real tournament list. card_text entries are short quotes from data/; see the full text there.

requirements: Real tournament list: load as many Grass Energy onto the board as possible; Hydrapple ex's attack scales with every Grass Energy you have in play, and Meganium makes each Grass Energy count twice.

cards.name: Teal Mask Ogerpon ex
cards.role: Energy engine and early attacker: attaches a Grass Energy from hand each turn and draws a card. Its attack also scales with Energy on both Active Pokémon.

cards.name: Chikorita
cards.role: Basic for Meganium.

cards.name: Bayleef
cards.role: Stage 1 for Meganium; its attack can push the opponent's Active to the Bench.

cards.name: Meganium
cards.role: Ability: every Basic Grass Energy on your Pokémon provides {G}{G}, doubling Syrup Storm's bonus. Wild Growth doesn't stack, so the 2nd copy is a backup for a Knock Out, not extra damage.

cards.name: Applin
cards.role: Basic for Hydrapple ex.

cards.name: Dipplin
cards.role: Stage 1 bridge to Hydrapple ex. Its Festival Lead Ability is unused because this list has no Festival Grounds; Do the Wave (20 per Benched Pokémon) is a backup attack.

cards.name: Hydrapple ex
cards.role: Main attacker. 330 HP; its Ability attaches another Grass Energy from hand each turn and heals 30, and its 2-Energy attack gains 30 damage for each Grass Energy attached to all your Pokémon.

cards.name: Fezandipiti ex
cards.role: Draws 3 after a Knock Out.

cards.name: Meowth ex
cards.role: Searches a Supporter when benched.

cards.name: Celebi
cards.role: Its 1-Energy attack searches up to 3 Grass Pokémon or Stadiums: a full evolution line from the Active Spot.

cards.name: Lillie's Determination
cards.role: Main draw Supporter.

cards.name: Boss's Orders
cards.role: Gusts a target to the Active Spot.

cards.name: Judge
cards.role: Both players shuffle away their hands and draw 4. Play it only after the Energy attachments for the turn, because it shuffles the Energy in your hand away too.

cards.name: Dawn
cards.role: Finds a Basic, a Stage 1 and a Stage 2 at once: a full Meganium or Hydrapple line.

cards.name: Lana's Aid
cards.role: Returns up to 3 non-Rule-Box Pokémon and Basic Energy from the discard pile to hand, rebuilding lines and Energy.

cards.name: Briar
cards.role: When the opponent has exactly 2 Prizes left, a Knock Out by your Tera Pokémon takes 1 extra Prize: can win the game a turn early.

cards.name: Ultra Ball
cards.role: Searches any Pokémon, including Hydrapple ex and Ogerpon.

cards.name: Bug Catching Set
cards.role: Looks at the top 7 cards for up to 2 Grass Pokémon or Basic Grass Energy: finds both evolutions and fuel.

cards.name: Poké Pad
cards.role: Searches any non-Rule-Box Pokémon: the evolution lines and Celebi.

cards.name: Night Stretcher
cards.role: Recovers a Pokémon or a Basic Energy.

cards.name: Unfair Stamp
cards.role: ACE SPEC comeback card after a Knock Out.

cards.name: Forest of Vitality
cards.role: Stadium: Grass Pokémon can evolve on the turn they were played (not on your first turn), which speeds up two Stage 2 lines.

cards.name: Grass Energy
cards.role: The fuel: Ogerpon and Hydrapple each attach one from hand every turn, and every one in play adds to Hydrapple's damage.

strategy: Teal Mask Ogerpon ex attaches extra Grass Energy and draws while Forest of Vitality, Dawn and Celebi rush out Meganium and Hydrapple ex. With three attachments a turn (manual, Ogerpon, Hydrapple), Grass Energy piles up fast, and Meganium doubles each one. Hydrapple ex's 2-Energy attack then gains 30 for every Grass Energy counted, so it Knocks Out anything, while its Ability heals 30 each turn and its 330 HP keeps it alive. Briar can steal an extra Prize to close the game.

main_resource.resource: Grass Energy attached across all your Pokémon (13 Grass Energy in the deck), counted by Syrup Storm
main_resource.formula: Syrup Storm: 30 + 30 per {G} Energy attached to all your Pokémon. With Meganium's Wild Growth each Basic Grass Energy provides {G}{G}, so 30 + 60 per card: 4 Energy = 270 (a 220 HP Pokémon ex), 5 = 330 (a 320 HP Dragapult ex), 6 = 390. Without Meganium it takes 10 Energy for 330. Hydrapple ex needs only 2 Energy of its own.

cards.name: Meganium
cards.effect: each Basic Grass Energy counts twice: +30 per card becomes +60 (does not stack, 2 copies)

cards.name: Teal Mask Ogerpon ex
cards.effect: +1 Grass attachment from hand each turn and draws 1 (4 copies)

cards.name: Hydrapple ex
cards.effect: Ripening Charge: +1 Grass attachment from hand each turn and heals 30 from that Pokémon

cards.name: Bug Catching Set
cards.effect: puts up to 2 Grass Pokémon or Basic Grass Energy from the top 7 into the hand (4 copies)

cards.name: Lana's Aid
cards.effect: returns up to 3 Pokémon and Basic Energy from the discard pile to the hand

cards.name: Night Stretcher
cards.effect: returns 1 Basic Energy from the discard pile

cards.name: Lillie's Determination
cards.effect: shuffles the hand away and draws 6 or 8; play it after attaching, not before

cards.name: Judge
cards.effect: shuffles both hands away: attach first, then play it

card_text: Hydrapple ex: "This attack does 30 more damage for each {G} Energy attached to all of your Pokémon."
Meganium: "Each Basic {G} Energy attached to all of your Pokémon provides {G}{G} Energy." ... "The effect of Wild Growth doesn't stack."
synergies.how_they_interact: The main engine. Each Grass Energy in play is +30 on Syrup Storm, and Meganium doubles every one of them to +60. Thresholds: 4 Energy = 270, 5 = 330, 6 = 390. A Hydrapple ex with 330 HP and 5 Energy on the board Knocks Out a 320 HP Pokémon ex alone. Wild Growth doesn't stack, so a second Meganium adds nothing in play: the second copy is only a backup for when the first is Knocked Out. Hydrapple ex attacks for 2 Energy, so it needs just 2 of the Energy on it and the rest can sit on other Pokémon.

card_text: Teal Mask Ogerpon ex: "you may attach a Basic {G} Energy card from your hand to this Pokémon" ... "draw a card"
Hydrapple ex: "you may attach a Basic {G} Energy card from your hand to 1 of your Pokémon" ... "heal 30 damage from that Pokémon"
Bug Catching Set: "Look at the top 7 cards of your deck. You may reveal up to 2 in any combination of {G} Pokémon and Basic {G} Energy cards"
Lana's Aid: "Put up to 3 in any combination of Pokémon that don't have a Rule Box and Basic Energy cards from your discard pile into your hand."
Judge: "Each player shuffles their hand into their deck and draws 4 cards."
synergies.how_they_interact: Three Grass Energy a turn (manual, Ogerpon, Hydrapple ex) is the ceiling, and every one has to be in hand. The deck has 13 Grass Energy in 60 cards, so the draw and recovery cards are what feed it: Ogerpon draws 1 when it attaches, Bug Catching Set takes up to 2 Energy from the top 7, Lana's Aid brings back up to 3 and Night Stretcher 1. Hydrapple ex also heals 30 from whatever it attaches to, so it keeps a damaged Ogerpon alive. Sequencing: attach everything first, then play Lillie's Determination or Judge, because both shuffle the hand (and the Energy in it) into the deck.

card_text: Forest of Vitality: "{G} Pokémon can evolve into {G} Pokémon during the turn they play those Pokémon, except during their first turn."
Celebi: "Search your deck for up to 3 in any combination of {G} Pokémon and Stadium cards"
Dawn: "Search your deck for a Basic Pokémon, a Stage 1 Pokémon, and a Stage 2 Pokémon"
synergies.how_they_interact: There are two Stage 2 lines (Chikorita - Bayleef - Meganium and Applin - Dipplin - Hydrapple ex) and only 1 Dawn and no Rare Candy. Forest of Vitality lets a Basic benched this turn evolve this turn, so each stage costs no extra turn. Celebi's attack from the Active Spot fetches Applin, Dipplin and Forest of Vitality (3 cards) in one go. Dawn finds a whole line, and Poké Pad and Ultra Ball fill what is missing. Limits: Forest also helps the opponent's Grass Pokémon, and it doesn't work on your first turn.

card_text: Briar: "You can use this card only if your opponent has exactly 2 Prize cards remaining." ... "take 1 more Prize card"
synergies.how_they_interact: Situational finisher. It needs the opponent to be on exactly 2 Prizes and the Knock Out to come from a Tera Pokémon's attack, so it is a 1-of. The list relies on Teal Mask Ogerpon ex and Hydrapple ex being Tera Pokémon; the card data doesn't mark Tera, so check the printed cards. When the opponent has exactly 2 Prizes left, a Syrup Storm that Knocks Out a Pokémon ex takes 2 + 1 = 3 Prizes in one turn.

card_text: Fezandipiti ex: "if any of your Pokémon were Knocked Out during your opponent's last turn, you may draw 3 cards"
Unfair Stamp: "you draw 5 cards, and your opponent draws 2 cards"
Meowth ex: "Search your deck for a Supporter card"
Bayleef: "Switch out your opponent's Active Pokémon to the Bench."
synergies.how_they_interact: The recovery package. After the opponent Knocks Out a Pokémon, Fezandipiti ex draws 3 and Unfair Stamp resets both hands (5 for you, 2 for them), which is the way to rebuild Energy in hand after a Knock Out on a Hydrapple ex. Meowth ex finds the Supporter that is missing (Briar, Dawn, Boss's Orders). Boss's Orders and Bayleef's Push Down choose or change what is Active.
